document: IStructE/Concrete Society Standard Method of Detailing Structural Concrete — Chapters 1–5
scope: GENERAL DETAILING INFORMATION — applies to all structural members

reinforcement_notation.standard_description_sequence: Number, type_and_grade, size, mark, bar_centres, location_or_comment

reinforcement_layering_notation.note: Contractor may not be familiar — illustrate with sketch on drawings

bar_mark_conventions.rule_1: Bar size is NOT part of the bar mark
bar_mark_conventions.rule_2: Prefixes/suffixes for location must not be included in bar mark
bar_mark_conventions.rule_3: Exception: varying shape/length bars may use letter suffixes, e.g. 8H20-1(a to h)-150
bar_mark_conventions.rule_4: Bar mark given on schedule for exception: 1a, 1b, 1c
bar_mark_conventions.rule_5: Same bar mark must never repeat within the same member name

schedule_reference_numbering.rule_zeros: The importance of leading zeros must be observed
schedule_reference_numbering.rule_uniqueness: Each schedule must have a different reference number and refer to only one drawing

bar_group_bar_marks_for_separate_drawing.note: When top and bottom reinforcement are detailed on separate drawings

mild_steel_grade_250.status: No longer commonly available in UK

fabric_reinforcement.scheduling: Separate fabric schedules from bar schedules, use BS 8666 fabric schedule form
fabric_reinforcement.where_same_fabric: Identify perimeter, note fabric type including orientation, layers, laps
fabric_reinforcement.sheet_count: Number of sheets in a set stated only once on drawing
fabric_reinforcement.layering_avoidance: Use 'flying end' fabrics or purpose-made fabrics

column_bar_link_retention.rule: Every column bar must be retained by a link
column_bar_link_retention.exception: Where distance between column bars is 150mm or less, every other bar should be retained by a link

column_bars_through_junction.rule: Column bars go straight through the junction

bottom_span_bars_at_column.rule: Bottom span bars stop short of column face

link_hanger_bars_at_column.rule: Link hanger bars stop short of column face

top_support_bars_primary_over_secondary.rule: Top support bars of primary beam are placed above secondary beam bars

continuity_through_column.rule: Continuity through column provided by main support bars and bottom support bars of appropriate sizes

vibrator_access.rule: Allow 75mm space for vibrator for every 300mm of beam width

cross_ties.rule: Cross ties at 1000mm centres to limit free height of link to 400mm

column_crank.rule: Column reinforcement cranked inside at crank ratio 1:10, with 50mm offset at kicker

secondary_beam_lever_arm.rule: Where secondary beam reinforcement has increased top cover, check resulting reduction in lever arm is satisfactory

beam_corner_detail.rule: Standard radius for both links and secondary beam reinforcement must pass between main reinforcement
beam_corner_detail.note: If corner bar must move, use smaller diameter to fit into radius of link — check with Designer

link_concrete_space.rule: Sufficient space between links to allow concrete and vibrator to pass through
link_concrete_space.note: When calculating actual space between links, add thickness of returned legs of link

large_column_centre_clear.rule: With large columns, advisable to keep central area free of links for formwork cleaning access prior to concreting

u_bars.rule: U-bars may be placed into column reinforcement for external (edge) beam-column connections
u_bars.position: U-bars must be positioned as close to far face of column as possible
u_bars.sequence: Bars fitted after column below cast, before prefabricated beam cage fixed in position

l_bars.rule: Where design requires L-bars with vertical leg fixed into lower column, position must be clearly shown on drawings
l_bars.note: Beam bottom L-bars cast into lower column before prefabricated beam cage placed in position
l_bars.warning: This detail can delay construction if reinforcement not fixed in correct position

flexible_detailing.definition: Method of detailing end bars separate from main longitudinal bars of an element
purpose: Ensures correct end cover achievable by limited telescoping at splice
flexible_detailing.example: Separate bottom splice bars at supports of continuous beams which lap onto main span bars

advantages: Improves speed and efficiency on site
Allows large proportion of reinforcement prefabrication
preformed_cages.notes: Decision to preassemble normally taken by Contractor; Designer and Detailer should bear possibility in mind

not_shown_on_reinforcement_drawings.rectangular: Up to 150x150mm in slabs or walls

holes_in_elements.must_be_shown: All other holes must be indicated on reinforcement drawing and trimmed where necessary

top_bottom_separate_drawings.rule: Separate drawings for top and bottom layers only for fabric and in exceptional cases (e.g. voided bridge decks, box girders with 4 layers)

reinforcement_cover_tolerances.rule: All reinforcement fixed to nominal cover using spacers of same nominal size as nominal cover
reinforcement_cover_tolerances.schedule_dimensions_for_bars_between_fac: Nominal concrete dimension less nominal cover on each face less allowance for other errors per Table 5.5
reinforcement_cover_tolerances.note_actual_bar_size: Actual size of bar is larger than nominal size — see 5.1.5

section_viewing_directions.rule: Sections taken consistently in same direction

flat_slab_reinforcement_areas_example.note: From Figure in Section 2.6, Example 1 — a marked-up GA for a flat slab showing required steel areas
flat_slab_reinforcement_areas_example.interpretation: These are required steel areas per mm width at specific grid locations in a real example flat slab
flat_slab_reinforcement_areas_example.status: DIRECTLY STATED (example only — not a general rule)
